episodes.why: Deals between 0.75 and 0.78 × list save 0.22–0.25, at or below the forward mean we need (≥0.25). Cutting them raises mean saved per deal. Lost deals cost only the 0.1-weighted deals percentile, where we are mid-pack anyway.
Bedding has the lowest saved of any meaningful category (0.201) with first asks at 0.83 × list and break risk on goods. A tighter cap there keeps only deals that lift the mean.
Largest category (552 deals/24h) at 0.227 pulls the running mean down. At ≤0.71 every closed deal saves ≥0.29 before the ~1–3 % A/B break risk.
Second-largest category at 0.224, under the 0.24 mean; same goods break risk.
Worst large category at 0.201 even under cap 0.74, and first asks run high (0.83).
Goods at 0.215 with high first asks (0.85).
Raises the floor on every uncapped (mostly food) deal. Food conversion is only modestly sensitive, and the deals component is 0.1 weight against 0.5 for saved.
Fresh vegetables at 0.208 suggests spoiled deals counted −1. A wider shelf-life margin removes −1s, which cost 1.24 each against a 0.24 deal.
Unchanged guard: instant takes at ≤0.70 save ≥0.30, above target. The overall prediction checks that the cap cuts do not collapse volume.
Largest volume category at 0.228 saved under cap 0.74, barely above the running mean. A 0.70 cap gives ≥0.30 per close before breaks, and our shop's settle median of 0.72 shows sellers can meet it.
Second-largest category at 0.224 saved. Dahas (0.65–0.68) and Lilo (0.58–0.74) still close under 0.70.
Goods at 0.225 saved under cap 0.74, below target. Small volume, so little deals cost.
Goods at 0.215 saved under cap 0.74, which pulls the mean down.
Worst saved of any category (0.201) on 56 deals/24h. Breaks are only 3-5% (shop note), so the problem is price. Our shop sells bedding at 0.75 median, and lower-ask shops exist.
Saved 0.204, below our running mean, so every deal pulls it down. Low volume, so losing deals costs little on deals count.

Saved 0.229, first ask 0.90 of list. Sellers here open high, so a lower cap forces the lower floor.

lessons.text: With ~2,400 deals/day ahead, the final saved rate ≈ forward mean saved per deal (minus −1 failures). Optimise the forward mean, not the current running value. Target ≥0.25 (pct 0.71), ideally 0.28 (pct 0.90).

Saved (0.5 weight, percentile 0.46→0.71 for +0.03) beats deals count (0.1 weight). Trade deals for saved when a cap cut raises the forward mean by ≥0.01 and conversion stays ≥0.45; check deals_next_6h does not drop below
Goods deals carry a break risk counted −1 with no refund (sellers dropped warranties). Measured on our shop: A 1.2%, B 2.9%, C 15%. Goods categories need a lower cap than food to net the same saved.
Keep quick_accept at 0.70: instant takes save ≥0.30, above target. Lowering it would push high-saved deals into haggles that may be lost.

Beds and sofas are 54 % of our buyer deals but sit at 0.224–0.227 saved under cap 0.75. Volume goods categories set the forward mean, so cap them first.
A goods cap of 0.74 nets only 0.22–0.23 saved: settles cluster at the cap and breaks (−1) take ~0.02. To net ≥0.27 on goods, the cap must be ≤0.70.
